content.title: 'From' season 4: Everything we know so far
content.text: (Image credit: MGM+) “From” fans, we’re not escaping the mystery just yet. That’s right, MGM Plus has confirmed that “From” will return for season 4. With season 3 leaving us with more questions than answers (as always), we’re all desperate to uncover the truth about the town, the creatures, and the residents still fighting to survive.Need a quick refresher? “From” is a gripping dark thriller that traps its characters in a nightmarish small town with no way out. As night falls, sinister, human-like creatures emerge, ruthlessly hunting anyone who happens to be trapped outside. With its unsettling atmosphere and shocking twists, “From” has cemented itself as a must-watch for horror lovers since its debut in 2022. What do you think? Who's your favorite character in From? During its explosive season 3 finale, “From” secured its spot as the #3 most talked-about show online and claimed the #1 position as the most-watched TV show on MGM Plus and Epix. It also has an impressive 96% score on Rotten Tomatoes and every season has maintained a rare streak of over 90% approval. Clearly, “From” stands out as one of the most consistently praised shows in recent years, which is why it became my favorite dark thriller on TV.Article continues below So, with season 3 leaving us with cliffhangers galore and fan theories running wild, it’s time to dive into what’s next. Here’s everything we know about “From” season 4, including the release date, cast updates, plot details and more.'From' season 4 confirmed release dateProduction on the new 10-episode season of "From" officially wrapped in Nova Scotia, where filming took place earlier in 2025. In an interview with Emmanuel Noisette, Jeff Pinkner (one of the executive producers) said: “There were a slew of rumors that the show would not be on the air until 2026. We're wildly hopeful that it will be on the air in 2025.” (h/t The Direct).However, another producer, John Griffin, was quick to correct that estimate: “Let me interject before we move on to the next question, if I may, because I don't want either Jeff or I to get hunted down by angry people. Jeff, correct me if I'm wrong, we're probably not going to be done shooting until the holidays. So in all likelihood, it would be early 2026, no?”Pinkner then confirmed it will probably be “early 2026.” This makes sense considering Deadline confirmed this release year when reporting the show’s renewal. And now, an official premiere date has been revealed: "From" season 4 is confirmed to debut on Sunday, April 19, 2026 on MGM+, meaning the spring prediction was correct. This timeline fits well with how the series has rolled out new seasons in the past.'From' season 4 episode guideHere’s the episode guide for "From" season 4, which is set to premiere on April 19, 2026 on MGM+ and will consist of 10 episodes that air weekly on Sundays. As of now, the episode titles haven’t been officially released:Episode 1 – Apr 19, 2026Episode 2 – Apr 26, 2026Episode 3 – May 3, 2026Episode 4 – May 10, 2026Episode 5 – May 17, 2026Episode 6 – May 24, 2026Episode 7 – May 31, 2026Episode 8 – Jun 7, 2026Episode 9 – Jun 14, 2026Episode 10 – Jun 21, 2026'From' season 4 cast As of August 26, 2025, it was revealed that "From" added a new series regular for season 4. Joining the cast is Julia Doyle, who will play Sophia. Deadline describes Sophia as "a sheltered and vulnerable pastor’s daughter."Beyond this brief character description, details are scarce, and fans will likely have to wait until the first full trailer to learn more about her role. (Image credit: Chris Reardon/MGM+)For “From” season 4, it’s safe to expect that Harold Perrineau will return as Boyd, the show’s central character. He'll again lead the charge in the town’s desperate fight for survival. Alongside Boyd, fans can also look forward to the likely return of key characters like Tabitha (Catalina Sandino Moreno), Julie (Hannah Cheramy), and Jade (David Alpay), who have all played crucial roles in the unfolding mystery.As for Eion Bailey’s character, Jim Matthews, the situation remains unclear. Jim met a brutal end in season 3, violently killed by the new villain, “The Man in Yellow,” who gruesomely slit his throat. However, with the introduction of time travel in the series, there’s a possibility that Jim’s story isn’t over yet. (Image credit: Chris Reardon/MGM+)Of course, other characters like Kenny (Ricky He), Victor (Scott McCord), Sara (Avery Konrad), Donna (Elizabeth Saunders), Ethan (Simon Webster) and Ellis (Corteon Moore) are bound to return. Ellis’ wife, Fatima (Pegah Ghafoori), seems to be safe after giving birth to one of the creatures, but she might be in danger again. As for Elgin (Nathan D. Simmons), the poor guy they tortured to learn the whereabouts of Fatima, isn’t in great condition right now. But he’ll probably recover and have some kind of revenge arc.Shaun Majumder could also return as Father Khatri. He died at the end of season 1, but Boyd has been hallucinating him ever since, even throughout season 3, when he was about to make a wrong decision. He may continue to hallucinate Father Khatri in the next season.Below is a list of characters who are likely to return in some capacity for “From” season 4:Harold Perrineau as Boyd StevensCatalina Sandino Moreno as Tabitha MatthewsHannah Cheramy as Julie MatthewsSimon Webster as Ethan MatthewsEion Bailey as Jim MatthewsDavid Alpay as Jade HerreraJulia Doyle as SophiaElizabeth Saunders as Donna RainesScott McCord as VictorRicky He as Kenny LiuChloe Van Landschoot as Kristi MillerPegah Ghafoori as Fatima HassanCorteon Moore as Ellis StevensAvery Konrad as Sara MyersKaelen Ohm as MarielleA.J. Simmons as RandallNathan D. Simmons as ElginRobert Joy as HenrySamantha Brown as AcostaShaun Majumder as Father Khatri (hallucination)'From' season 4 plot (Image credit: Chris Reardon/MGM+)The final episode of “From” season 3 revealed a lot, yet still left us with plenty of lingering mysteries. The most significant revelation, however, is the true nature of the creatures that terrorize the town each night. Once human, these beings sacrificed their children in exchange for eternal life — though it’s clear that immortality comes at a horrifying cost. Fatima, for instance, was pregnant with Smiley, the creature Boyd killed, showing how these beings can return even after death. This is the chilling price they pay for their twisted version of eternal life.Then, we were introduced to the Man in Yellow, who appears to be the central villain moving forward — and possibly the mastermind behind the creation of this nightmarish town. He’s responsible for Jim’s death at the end of season 3, clearly intent on stopping anyone from uncovering the town’s dark secrets.Another major revelation is that Julie is undoubtedly time-traveling. In the episode’s final moments, when she finds her father, her appearance has changed — her hair is shorter, and she’s wearing different clothes. She desperately warns him to run, saying, “This is when it happens.” It’s clear she’s been through multiple timelines, trying to alter the course of events to save her father, but so far, her attempts have been in vain. (Image credit: Chris Reardon/MGM+)Given what we've learned, it’s clear that Julie will play a crucial role in navigating different timelines in season 4, likely working to prevent horrific events from unfolding. She may even travel back to the past to uncover the truth behind the parents’ sacrifice of their children and, more importantly, who they made their dark bargain with — likely the Man in Yellow.Boyd now understands that the creatures can be reborn, and he’s beginning to piece together the eerie connection to the ghostly Kimono Lady who tormented Fatima, hinting that she may hold the key to the creatures' resurrection.For now, we’ll have to sit with the lingering questions season 3 left us with and patiently wait for an official synopsis for “From” season 4. However, we will likely not see a teaser until the end of 2025, so the suspense will continue a little longer.'From' season 4 trailers/teasersThe first official "From" season 4 trailer dropped alongside the announcement of its April 19, 2026 premiere date. This brief teaser puts the show’s creeping dread front and center, while highlighting the overarching theme that “knowledge comes at a cost,” a line that acts both as a tagline and a warning about the dangers lurking within the town’s mysteries.Though it doesn’t reveal major twists, the footage leans into ominous visuals and unsettling hints that the residents’ search for answers will only pull them deeper into terror and uncertainty. Fans also catch glimpses of the Man in the Yellow Suit and other eerie elements, suggesting that the new season will expand on the mythology and horrors that have defined the series so far. FROM Season 4 (MGM+ 2026 Series) Official Trailer - YouTube Watch On Finally, we have a full-length trailer for "From" season 4. The latest preview heightens the mystery and dread surrounding the eerie, trapped town at the center of the series, promising that the residents’ hunt for answers won’t get any easier — and that uncovering the truth may come at a terrifying cost.The trailer’s official synopsis leans into several of the show’s biggest lingering questions, including the true nature of the Man in Yellow’s intentions, what revelations Jade and Tabitha may have uncovered, and just how far Boyd’s body and mind can go before they break under pressure.Visually and tonally, the footage only builds upon the horror atmosphere that fans have come to expect. It’s clear that Season 4 will dig deeper into the mythos of the town, the mysterious forces at play, and the psychological fraying of those still trying to survive its nightmare loop. 1 of 5 How would you handle waking up in a strange town you can’t escape? 2 of 5 What scares you the most? 3 of 5 How do you make decisions under pressure? 4 of 5 The town offers you one way out but it means leaving others behind.
